@intent_handler("sound_like.intent")
def handle_sound_like(self, message):
    subject = (message.data.get("subject") or "").strip()
    if not subject:
        self.speak_dialog("sound_not_found", {"subject": subject})
        return

    bundled = self._bundled_sound_path(subject, self.lang)
    if bundled:
        # instant=True: no preceding speech, so it should play
        # immediately rather than queue
        self.play_audio(bundled, instant=True)
        return

    if not self.api_key:
        self.speak_dialog("no_online_lookup", {"subject": subject})
        return

    if not is_connected():
        self.speak_dialog("offline_no_internet", {"subject": subject})
        return

    # Speak first, so the network round-trip doesn't feel like
    # dead air - then queue (not instant) so playback follows the
    # speech rather than potentially talking over it.
    self.speak_dialog("searching_online", {"subject": subject})
    try:
        url = self._search_freesound(subject)
    except Exception:
        self.log.exception(f"freesound lookup failed for {subject!r}")
        self.speak_dialog("sound_lookup_failed", {"subject": subject})
        return

    if not url:
        self.speak_dialog("sound_not_found", {"subject": subject})
        return

    self.play_audio(url, instant=False)

entries.text: Hvordan lyder en ko? Bundlede offline-lyde (i dag dyr) for øjeblikkelige svar, med et valgfrit freesound.org online-fallback for alt andet, filtreret til kun CC0-licenserede resultater.
How does a cow sound? Bundled offline sounds (currently animals) for instant answers, with an optional freesound.org online fallback for anything else, filtered to CC0-licensed results.
what does a dog sound like

Struktur: kategori -> {talt ord: filnavn (uden filtype) i sounds/<kategori>/}. Kategori-inddelt ligesom ovos-skill-convert - kun 'animals' findes lige nu, men skillet er ikke dyre-specifikt (se README), det er bare den bundlede kerneliste der er dyr i dag.
Alt der ikke findes her falder igennem til freesound.org-fallback - se __init__.py.

Structure: category -> {spoken word: bundled sound filename (no extension, lives in sounds/<category>/)}. This is deliberately category-grouped like the ovos-skill-convert project's unit_aliases.json, even though only one category (animals) exists so far - the skill is NOT animal-specific (see README), the bundled/offline set just happens to be animals today. Adding a new bundled category later (e.g. 'landmarks', 'weather') means adding a new top-level key here plus matching files in sounds/<category>/, no code changes.
Anything not found here falls through to the freesound.org fallback - see __init__.py.
